purpose: Backing data + provenance for an interactive HPRC data-availability web app.
authoritative_source: s3://human-pangenomics (enumerated directly). GitHub org tables used for metadata and explanation only.

files.data/hprc_catalog.json: Compact payload for a static app. Per-sample modality lists, totals, intersections. 114 KB - ship as-is, no backend needed.
files.data/hprc_sample_modality_matrix.csv: 438 samples x 14 modality booleans + release/population/sex/n_modalities. Same content as the JSON, tabular.
files.data/hprc_file_index.csv: 19,807 rows: one per data file. sample_id, modality, assay_detail, s3_key, https_url, size_bytes, source, indexed_on_github. Use for per-sample download lists.
files.data/hprc_modality_intersections.csv: Precomputed counts for 8 useful modality combinations.
files.data/hprc_assay_provenance.csv: Per modality: which GitHub index covers it, whether S3 is the only source, caveats.
files.data/hprc_samples_not_in_any_release_tab: Samples with primary data that no release index references.
files.scripts/build_hprc_catalog.py: Regenerates everything above from S3 + GitHub. ~2 min. Run when HPRC adds data.

app_features_supported.browse_by_category: Filter hprc_catalog.json samples[] by modality membership.
app_features_supported.search_by_sample: Index samples[] by sample_id; modalities[] is the answer.
app_features_supported.combine_modalities: Boolean AND across modality columns. Precomputed common cases in intersections.
app_features_supported.download_lists: Join sample_id + modality into hprc_file_index.csv, present https_url.

critical_caveats: GitHub index tables are NOT comprehensive. They resolve ~10.3k of 19.8k data files. Eight modalities (FiberSeq, MicroC, ONT_directRNA, Bionano, Microarray, Karyotype, StrandSeq, TenX) have NO GitHub index at all - S3 is the only source.
indexed_on_github=False does not mean the data is unofficial. It often means the file postdates the last index refresh, or the assay was never indexed.
Micro-C exists for exactly one sample (HG002) and is raw fastq only.

ONT chromatin-stenciling 6mA basecalls are a Fiber-seq basecall variant living inside the UCSC ONT Fiber-seq submission - NOT a separate assay. Tracked via assay_detail and the FiberSeq_ONT_stenciling flag. Do not present as its own modality.
Do NOT filter S3 objects by file extension when rebuilding. Doing so silently drops Bionano, karyotype, microarray, and HG002 Strand-seq (.txt.gz).
release column: R2/R3/untagged. 'untagged' means the sample has data but no row in either release metadata table - surface this, do not hide it.
Multi-modal analyses are ~100-sample studies: 346 samples have the 5 core modalities, only 100 add Fiber-seq, only 44 also have HiFi 5mC.
next_phase: Both cohorts catalogued. Remaining: wire the app; optionally add the separate 718-sample pooled Strand-seq 1kGP cohort as a third facet.
key_contrast: HGSVC3 is small but near-complete: 64/69 samples carry 8 modalities. HPRC is large but sparse beyond the core five: 346/438 have the core 5, only ~100 add Fiber-seq. HGSVC3 has short-read RNA-seq (67 samples); HPRC has none. HPRC has Fiber-seq (111), HiFi 5mC (86) and Micro-C (1); HGSVC3 has none of those.
